title: Burial and peace
summary: After the people of Ammon were established in Jershon and the Lamanites were driven out, the dead were buried. Days of fasting, mourning, and prayer followed. In the sixteenth year of the judges, continual peace began throughout the land.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon, and the Lamanites were driven out of the land.
The people of the land buried the Lamanites' dead.
Neither the Lamanites' dead nor the Nephites' dead were numbered.
After the burials and days of fasting, mourning, and prayer, continual peace began throughout the land in the sixteenth year of the reign of the judges.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Burial activity or people mourning may be shown as separate moments, without depicting bodies in detail.
unspecified_visual_details: The burial locations, burial customs, clothing, and identities of individual mourners are unspecified.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The burial, days of fasting, mourning, and prayer, and beginning of peace occur in sequence, not as one simultaneous moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the driving out as a present-tense battle.
Do not specify where the Nephites' dead were buried.
Do not identify the Lamanites as belonging to another era.

explicit_facts.text: The people observed the commandments of the Lord and the ordinances of God according to the law of Moses.
There was no disturbance throughout the sixteenth year, and continual peace at the commencement of the seventeenth year.

unspecified_visual_details: The specific ordinances, gathering place, participants, and time of day are unspecified.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unspecified ordinance as a particular ritual.

title: A man comes to Zarahemla
summary: In the latter end of the seventeenth year, a man comes into the land of Zarahemla and begins preaching against prophecies concerning the coming of Christ.

explicit_facts.text: In the latter end of the seventeenth year, a man came into the land of Zarahemla and began preaching to the people against prophecies concerning the coming of Christ.
There was no law against a man’s belief, and people were on equal grounds under the law.
The scripture says, “Choose ye this day, whom ye will serve.”
A person could serve God if he believed in God, and disbelief was not punishable by law.
Murder, robbery, theft, and adultery were punishable; people were judged according to their crimes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The man may be shown addressing people in the land of Zarahemla.
unspecified_visual_details: The man’s appearance and clothing, the audience’s appearance, and the setting’s architecture are unspecified.

Choose ye this day, whom ye will serve.

prohibited_inventions: Do not name the man Korihor from verses outside the supplied source.

explicit_facts.text: Korihor began to preach to the people that there should be no Christ.
The law could have no hold upon Korihor.
Korihor questioned the people's hope and why they looked for a Christ.
Korihor called prophecies foolish traditions of their fathers.
Korihor argued that they could not know there would be a Christ.

unspecified_visual_details: The location, Korihor's appearance, and the listeners' appearance and responses are unspecified.

title: The preacher's claims
summary: A man challenges belief in remission of sins. He denies atonement, teaches that people prosper through their abilities and conquer through strength, and declares that no conduct is a crime. His preaching leads many astray, and he teaches that death is the end.
characters: male preacher whose name is not supplied

explicit_facts.text: The speaker attributes belief in remission of sins to a frenzied mind and ancestral traditions.

He teaches that no atonement can be made for sins, that people fare according to their management, prosper according to their genius, and conquer according to their strength, and that whatever a person does is no crime.
The narrator reports that his preaching leads many into wickedness and leads many women and men to commit whoredoms.
He teaches that death is the end.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The preacher may be shown addressing listeners without individualized reactions.
unspecified_visual_details: Location, clothing, physical appearances, audience size, and spatial arrangement are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: male preacher whose name is not supplied

narration.text: And thus he did preach unto them, leading away the hearts of many,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied verses do not name the preacher. The audit's identification relies on preceding verses not supplied here and cannot establish his name under the source-only constraint.
The preacher's claims are attributed teachings, not established doctrinal facts.
The reported consequences of his preaching must not become separate enacted incidents or be portrayed as simultaneous audience behavior.
prohibited_inventions: Do not import names or identifying details from unsupplied verses.
Do not invent a location, listener biographies, dialogue, or individual conversions.
Do not stage sexual acts, deaths, or conquests from the summarized consequences and teachings.
Do not literalize leading away hearts or invent supernatural appearances.

summary: High priest Giddonah questions Korihor about preaching against the Lord's ways, Christ, and the prophets. Korihor responds that he rejects what he calls his hearers’ foolish traditions and ordinances.

summary: Korihor continues his response, accusing the religious teachers of keeping the people in bondage and asserting that a child is not guilty because of its parents. He disputes their claims about Christ and prophecy.

title: Alma answers the accusation
summary: Alma says he has supported himself through his own labor and received no payment for church labor. He asks why Korihor accuses them of preaching for gain and whether their teaching deceives the people.

explicit_facts.text: Alma said he had worked with his own hands for support while traveling to declare God's word.
Alma said he had received no senine for church labor, and his brethren had received payment only according to law for time in the judgment seat.
Alma said their purpose in laboring in the church was to declare truth and rejoice in their brethren's joy.
Alma asked why Korihor accused them of preaching for gain and whether Korihor believed they deceived the people.
